::: {#def-batch-norm}

#### Batch normalization

**Batch normalization** rescales each [pre-activation](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-pre-activation) of a layer across the examples of a minibatch.
For a minibatch of $B$ examples,
let $z_{ij}$ be pre-activation $j$ for example $i$,
with mean and variance over the minibatch

$$
\mu_j = \frac{1}{B} \sumto{i}{B} z_{ij},
\qquad
\sigma_j^2 = \frac{1}{B} \sumto{i}{B} \paren{z_{ij} - \mu_j}^2.
$$

Batch normalization replaces $z_{ij}$ with

$$
\gamma_j \frac{z_{ij} - \mu_j}{\sqrt{\sigma_j^2 + \smallconst}} + \beta_j,
$$

where $\gamma_j$ and $\beta_j$ are [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) learned with the rest,
and $\smallconst$ is a small constant that keeps the division finite
[@ioffe2015batch; @goodfellow2016deep, section 8.7.1].
When the network makes predictions,
running averages of $\mu_j$ and $\sigma_j^2$ from training take the place of the minibatch's.
PyTorch's running average of the variance divides by $B - 1$ instead of $B$ [@pytorch_batchnorm1d].

:::
